subject: Follow-up: Competitive TCO comparison vs hyperscalers + proposed next tests
messages:
From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@meridian.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks - competitive TCO follow-up & proposed test plan

Hi Emily - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Recap:
- Primary goal: reduce inference unit costs for your summarization pipeline while keeping p95 latency under 400ms for interactive workflows.
- Current infra: self-hosted Mistral 7B on GCP with nginx routing; ~1.2M tokens/day across customers; observed 20% variability in latency during peaks.
- Competitive concerns: comparing Redwood runtime vs your current setup and hyperscaler options (AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI) - both cost and reliability matter.

What I promised to follow up with:
1) A short TCO sketch for per-1M tokens comparing Redwood hosted/dedicated vs hyperscaler-managed endpoints and basic self-hosted numbers - attached as redwood_tco_calc_v1.xlsx.
2) A proposed 2-week test plan to run apples-to-apples perf and unit-econ tests (details below).

Why Redwood matters here (short):
- Optimized serving runtime that reduces effective token compute cost through batching + prefix/KV caching + quantization-friendly kernels.
- Smart routing & fallbacks to lower-cost variants when SLAs permit.

Proposed test plan (start next week):
A) 100k-token baseline run against your canonical workload on three configs: Redwood hosted (13B quantized), AWS Bedrock (managed), and current self-hosted. Measure: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens (extrapolated).
B) Cache-effect test: replay 10k user sessions with realistic prefix overlap to estimate prefix cache hit rate and resulting cost delta.
C) Batching sensitivity: run synthetic load at batch sizes 1, 4, 16 to see throughput vs latency tradeoffs.

Quick unit-econ thumbnail from the attached spreadsheet (high-level assumptions in sheet):
- Hyperscaler-managed (example): nominal list inference cost ~ $120 / 1M tokens (variable by model), no prefix caching assumed.
- Self-hosted (your current): raw infra-only compute + ops amortized ~ $45 / 1M tokens (but higher ops burden and variability).
- Redwood hosted (optimized, with 30% prefix cache hit & 2x effective batching): projected $28 / 1M tokens (net) - see calc tab for inputs.

Next steps I suggest:
- Can we lock the 2-week test window starting Tue 2026-03-10?
- Please confirm which dataset/samples you want us to run (full production sample or redacted subset).

I attached the TCO calc + a PDF with initial benchmark snippets (bench_results_raw_0308.pdf). Happy to sync with Raj if he wants to join the test plan.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Thanks - competitive TCO follow-up & proposed test plan

Thanks Aditya - useful recap and appreciated the spreadsheet. A few clarifying Qs before we commit to the run window: 

1) The $28 / 1M tokens number - can you show the raw assumptions (GPU type, SLO load, token mix for prompt vs completion)? The sheet has some but please confirm the exact GPU/instance footprint you're modeling.
2) For the cache-effect test, our prefix repetition varies a lot by customer. Average expected prefix reuse is around 22% for support threads but up to 48% for our internal knowledge base flows. Can the test simulate that distribution?
3) Who will own the test orchestration? Will Redwood pull logs or do we provide an anonymized event stream?

We're open to Tue 03/10 - prefer morning PT. We'll provide a redacted sample session set (50k tokens) that mirrors production.

Emily Zhao
Head of AI Products | Meridian AI
emily.zhao@meridian.ai
415-555-0102

From: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@meridian.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks - competitive TCO follow-up & proposed test plan

Emily - great questions. Answers inline + updated plan: 

1) GPU / instance assumptions: the calc uses NVIDIA A10G equivalent for self-hosted and dedicated math, and a quantized 13B on NVIDIA H100-like perf assumptions for Redwood-hosted path (we model 4-bit quantized kernels + batching). Sheet tab 'assumptions' lists: H100-equivalent throughput for quantized 13B = ~600 tokens/sec per GPU under 16 batch; A10G-equivalent for self-hosted = ~220 tokens/sec per GPU under 8 batch. We can switch to exact GCP SKU numbers if you prefer.

2) Cache simulation: yes - we can run three replay profiles (low/med/high reuse) matching your 22%/35%/48% buckets and report hit rates and cost deltas. We'll also surface the prefix length distribution effects.

3) Orchestration: Redwood can run the tests on a hosted sandbox you approve (we'll only use redacted inputs). We will provide the raw perf logs (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU util, cache hit events). If you prefer to run on-prem, we can provide a harness you run and upload results.

Proposed refinement to the timeline:
- Tue 03/10 AM PT: kickoff & handoff of sample data + confirm run profiles.
- Wed-Thu: run baseline 3-way tests (Redwood hosted, Bedrock, self-hosted).
- Fri: cache-effect & batching sensitivity runs + deliver initial report.

Action: Emily, can you share the redacted sample by end-of-day Monday? We'll schedule the kickoff for Tue 9:30am PT.

I'll loop in Marcus (solutions eng) to define exact metrics we should capture.

Thanks,
Aditya

From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-03-08T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: test checklist + quick model/config notes

Quick internal note for the run (for Aditya/LAuren to agree before kickoff):

Checklist:
- Confirm sample dataset format (JSONL sessions) and that PII is redacted.
- Confirm target SLOs: interactive p95 <= 400ms, throughput target 2k tokens/sec sustained for baseline.
- Prepare run matrix:
  * Redwood-hosted: 13B quantized (4-bit), batching 4/16, prefix caching enabled (LRU TTL default).
  * AWS Bedrock: equivalent managed model (use their recommended endpoint), batching as allowed by service.
  * Self-hosted: current Mistral 7B on GCP, your tune/optimizations.
- Instrumentation: include token-level cost logs + GPU utilization + cache hit markers.

Initial perf & TCO heuristics (to reference in call):
- Effective batching gains: moving from batch=1 to batch=16 can reduce per-token GPU compute cost by ~2.1x in our kernels for 13B models (depends on payload).
- Prefix cache sensitivity: each +10% absolute cache hit reduces total tokens forwarded to model by 10%, so direct proportional cost drop; realistic net saving also depends on average prefix length and whether cached KV fits memory.
- Example worked calc for 1M end-user tokens/month (production mix):
  * Raw model tokens (no cache): 1,000,000 -> compute cost baseline on A100-style = $60 (GPU amortized) + $10 infra/ops = $70 => ~ $70 / 1M tokens.
  * With 30% prefix hit and batching optimizations: compute load -> 700k model tokens -> effective compute cost = $42 + infra $8 = $50 -> ~$50 / 1M.
  * Redwood hosted w/ optimized runtime + additional queueing/batching -> further efficiency -> projected ~$28-$32 / 1M (this aligns with Aditya's sheet).

I'll prepare the run harness and a short readme for Emily. Also let's be ready to highlight fallback policies (cheaper model variants automatically used when p95 headroom > X ms).

Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
